title: Retest of a broken level
description: Price returns to within retest_tolerance_atr_multiple of ATR of a level that HERMES reports as recently broken, no more than max_bars_since_break bars after the break, and when require_close_on_break_side is true closes back on the side the break travelled towards. The broken level, its direction and its age are HERMES-supplied market facts, not the output of another HSA strategy.
thesis: A level that has been broken and then revisited without being reclaimed has been tested as support or resistance in its new role. The revisit is what converts a break into evidence rather than a single excursion.

required_hermes_fields.purpose: Price of the structural level HERMES most recently reports as broken.
Side the break travelled towards, UP or DOWN, as reported by HERMES.
Bars elapsed since that break, counted on the evaluated timeframe.
High of the evaluated bar, used to measure the revisit after a downward break.
Low of the evaluated bar, used to measure the revisit after an upward break.
Close of the evaluated bar, used by require_close_on_break_side.
Average true range over atr_period, used to scale the retest tolerance.

parameters.name: retest_tolerance_atr_multiple
parameters.description: Maximum distance between the revisiting extreme and the broken level, as a multiple of ATR, for the bar to count as a retest.

parameters.name: max_bars_since_break
parameters.description: Maximum number of bars between the break and the retest. Beyond this the revisit is treated as unrelated to the break.

parameters.name: require_close_on_break_side
parameters.description: When true the evaluated bar must close on the side the break travelled towards, so a retest that reclaims the level does not match.

parameters.name: atr_period
parameters.description: Lookback of the average true range used to scale the retest tolerance, in bars of the evaluated timeframe.

direction_semantics.direction_rule: LONG when level.recent_break_direction is UP and the bar low returns to within tolerance of the level from above; SHORT when it is DOWN and the bar high returns to within tolerance from below.

fields.name: matched
fields.description: True when the revisit, its age and the close-side condition all hold.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: LONG after an upward break, SHORT after a downward break.

fields.name: level_price
fields.description: Price of the broken level the retest was measured against.

fields.name: retest_distance_atr
fields.description: Distance from the revisiting extreme to that level, divided by ATR.

fields.name: bars_since_break
fields.description: Bars elapsed between the break and the evaluated bar.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Each condition, its threshold and whether it held.

deterministic_test_cases.description: Bar low returns to 1.0 above the level with an ATR of 8.0, a distance of 0.125 ATR, six bars after an upward break, closing above the level.
Bar high returns to 1.0 below the level with an ATR of 8.0, four bars after a downward break, closing below the level.
Bar low stops 6.0 above the level with an ATR of 8.0, a distance of 0.75 ATR, outside the 0.25 tolerance.
The revisit is inside the price tolerance but arrives 40 bars after the break, past the 24-bar bound.
Price revisits the level inside tolerance but closes back on the opposite side, so require_close_on_break_side rejects it.

provenance.source_reference: PID.md line 55 — retest, named as a canonical atomic strategy for HSA v1.
provenance.notes: Architect-set defaults. Boundary call recorded deliberately: the broken level is consumed as a HERMES fact (level.recent_break_price and its companions), not as the output of structure_break. Taking it from another HSA strategy would make this entry aware of a peer and would breach PID line 59; taking it from HERMES keeps it independently testable against fixed facts. A chain that wants the two to agree composes them, it does not wire them together.
